persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Achieng, 19, selling mandazi from a small stall near the bus stage in Kisumu. Every month you work hard, but at the end of the month there is almost nothing left. Today you want to know: how many mandazi must I sell before I stop losing money, and is my price too low?

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Break-Even. In about three minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. Many small sellers choose a price by guessing. They copy the price of the next stall, or they choose a round number.
Then they work hard the whole month, but at the end there is almost no money left, and they do not know why.
The answer is usually in three numbers. Break-Even asks for those three numbers, and gives you one honest answer.
Who uses it? Anyone who sells something: mandazi, phone covers, clothes from a tailor. The maths is the same everywhere.
One important thing. The app was made in America, so the boxes say dollars. You can type Kenya shillings instead. The answer works exactly the same way. Just remember the money is shillings.

lines.t: Number one: your price. How much the customer pays you for one item. This is the first box, called Average price per sale.

Number two: what one item costs you to make or buy. For mandazi, that is the flour, the oil and the sugar for one mandazi. This is the second box, called Variable cost per sale. Variable means it goes up when you sell more.

Number three: the costs you must pay every month, even if you sell nothing. Stall rent. Charcoal. Your phone bundle for the business. Add them all together. This is the third box, called Monthly fixed costs. Fixed means it does not change with sales.

lines: Be careful here. This is the most common mistake. Rent does not go in the second box. Rent is paid once a month, so it goes in the third box. Flour is used for every single mandazi, so it goes in the second box.

lines.t: As soon as you type, the answers appear below. You do not press any button. The app saves your numbers on this phone by itself.
The first answer is Sales needed per month. This is the big one. It is how many items you must sell in a month before you stop losing money. Below that number, you lose. Above it, you make a profit.
You keep per sale is your price minus what one item costs you. This small amount is what pays your rent, little by little.

lines: Let us try an example together. A mandazi sells for 10 shillings. One mandazi costs 6 shillings to make. So you keep 4 shillings on each one.
The stall rent is 1,500 shillings a month, and charcoal is 900. Together that is 2,400 shillings every month.
2,400 divided by 4 is 600. So you must sell 600 mandazi a month just to cover your costs. That is 20 every day, before you earn anything for yourself.

lines.t: Now look at the table at the bottom. It is called If your price were. It shows what happens if you change your price by ten or twenty percent, up or down.

lines: Each row shows a different price, and how many sales you would need at that price. A small change in price can make a very big change in the sales you need.

If the price is lower than what one item costs you, the app shows a red message. It means you lose money on every sale, and no number of sales can save you. The fix is always to raise the price above your cost.
Your numbers stay only on this phone. There is no account, and nothing is sent to anyone.
To start again with empty boxes, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap Start fresh. The app asks you twice before it erases anything.
That is all. Three numbers in: price, cost of one item, and monthly costs. One answer out: how many sales you need.
In the test, you will be a mandazi seller. Think like a seller, take your time, and if something is confusing, say so. Confusing parts are exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Achieng with the mandazi stall. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press — use what you learned. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Break-Even. If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The three boxes are now empty. (Verified 10 Oct: all four checks false after this.)

tasks.text: One mandazi costs you: flour 4 shillings, oil 1.50 and sugar 0.50. Put in what ONE mandazi costs you to make.
tasks.hint: Add the three costs for one mandazi together (4 + 1.50 + 0.50). It goes in the box for the cost of ONE sale, not the monthly box.

tasks.text: Every month you pay stall rent of 1,500 shillings and charcoal of 900 shillings. Put in your monthly costs.
tasks.hint: Rent and charcoal are paid every month even if you sell nothing. Add them together and put the total in the monthly box.

tasks.text: You can sell about 15 mandazi a day — 450 a month — and customers will not pay more than 15 shillings. Set a price that covers all your costs with 450 sales a month or fewer.
tasks.hint: Look at 'Sales needed / month' as you change the price. It must be 450 or less, and the price must be 15 or less.

tasks.text: Find the LOWEST whole-shilling price that still covers all your costs with 450 sales a month. Leave that price in the app.
tasks.hint: Try prices one shilling at a time (11, 12, 13…) and watch 'Sales needed / month'. Pick the smallest price where it is 450 or less.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: tells you how many sales you need before you stop losing money
uses your price, the cost of one item, and your monthly costs
lets you test a different price before you change it

daily.task: Try one new number in Break-Even (a new price or a new cost) and look at the answer.
